body_html:
How to think about it

Things are made from raw materials. Plants give cotton, jute, wood and bamboo; animals give wool, silk, milk and honey; the earth gives clay, sand, iron and stone. Cotton is picked, cleaned, spun into thread and woven into cloth. Clay is kneaded, shaped on a potter's wheel, dried and baked in a kiln.

Sugarcane juice is boiled to make jaggery; cream is churned to make butter; wood pulp is pressed into paper. Artisans such as potters, weavers and carpenters make things by hand. Reuse and recycle things, because making them uses materials, energy and hard work.

Example

Glass is made from…

heated until it melts

Answer: sand

Example

Just after spinning comes…

thread → cloth

Answer: weaving

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up spinning and weaving.
  • Thinking paper comes from cotton.
  • Thinking clay pots are baked before they are shaped.

faq.q: What is the difference between spinning and weaving?
faq.a: Spinning twists fibres into thread; weaving crosses threads to make cloth.

faq.q: Why are clay pots baked in a kiln?
faq.a: Baking makes the clay hard and strong so the pot does not crumble in water.
